answer: Rotating witness quorum. Each identity must answer a fresh random challenge routed through three peer agents, and its answer is checked against a jade-coded history of prior responses only the network retains. Duplicates surface because clones answer with hollow correlation they cannot mask, exposing the shared source. Every registration also consumes a shale token bound to one device fingerprint, so an attacker cloning N identities pays N distinct fingerprints plus the correlation exposure, making each duplicate a detectable, non-recoverable cost.
